definitions.explanation: An item of excellent quality or historical significance, renowned for its craftsmanship or artistic value. Often used in the context of art, antiques, traditional crafts, and gourmet food.

examples.japanese: この{茶碗|ちゃわん}は{名品|めいひん}だ。
examples.english: This tea bowl is a renowned masterpiece.

examples.japanese: {各地|かくち}の{名品|めいひん}を{集|あつ}めた{展覧会|てんらんかい}が{開|ひら}かれる。
examples.english: An exhibition gathering fine articles from various regions will be held.

examples.japanese: この{美術館|びじゅつかん}には{国宝級|こくほうきゅう}の{名品|めいひん}が{数多|かずおお}く{所蔵|しょぞう}されている。
examples.english: This museum houses many fine pieces of national treasure caliber.

notes:
Refers to items that are widely recognized for their excellence — whether works of art, traditional crafts, gourmet specialties, or luxury goods. The word emphasizes fame and recognition of quality. Often used in department store promotions ({全国|ぜんこく}{名品|めいひん}{展|てん}, exhibition of fine products from across Japan) and museum contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {名品|めいひん}{展|てん} — exhibition of fine articles
- {全国|ぜんこく}の{名品|めいひん} — fine products from across the country
- {名品|めいひん}ぞろい — a lineup of masterpieces
- {名品|めいひん}を{鑑賞|かんしょう}する — to appreciate fine works

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {逸品|いっぴん} — excellent item; emphasizes quality rather than fame; more about personal judgment of excellence
- {傑作|けっさく} — masterpiece; typically used for creative works (art, literature, film)
- {銘品|めいひん} — also read めいひん, written with a different first character; refers to famous branded products, often local specialties
